Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Short answers first, then an example and attachments.

Summary answers:
- Billing unit: We bill on consumed tokens per request (input + output) with an additional context-flooring mechanism for long pinned sessions. That means you pay for tokens generated/ingested each call, but long-context sessions can trigger a context-slab charge if the runtime keeps >N tokens resident across calls (see example).
- Caching: KV/prefix cache reuse reduces billable input because repeated prefixes are not re-encoded every call — we apply a cache-reuse credit that exempts repeated token sequences from the input token charge up to the cached prefix length.
- Rounding/minimums: We round per-request up to the token quantum (default 8 tokens for streaming, 16 for non-streaming calls) and we apply a per-session microfloor if a session has fewer than 5 calls in a billing window to avoid abuse. For committed Dedicated customers we can waive the microfloor.
- Discounts: Standard commit tiers: 0–5M: base; 5–20M: 10% off; 20–50M: 18% off; >50M: 25% off. Pilot concessions are negotiable — see Kimberly's note below.

Attached: billing_examples.xlsx with worked examples and a small pilot_pricing_matrix.csv. Quick worked example (matches the spreadsheet):

Scenario: 52,000-token session + two keepalives (10 tokens each)
1) Session: a single call where the model returns a 52k token response (split into streaming chunks). Billable tokens = 52,000 output + input tokens for that call (assume 5,000 input) = 57,000 tokens.
2) Keepalives: two separate non-streaming heartbeat requests at 10 tokens each => rounded up to token quantum 16 => billable 16 + 16 = 32 tokens.
3) Context-slab: because the session stores a 52k context, the platform applies a context-slab charge: we bill an additional slab of 50k tokens once per billing window for retained context above the default long-context threshold (we prorate slab charges daily). For Dedicated customers the slab is discounted and can be amortized against commit credits.

Invoice line example (monthly):
- Redwood LLM - usage (input+output): 57,032 tokens @ $0.00012/token = $6.84
- Context slab retention (50k slab proration for month): 50,000 tokens @ $0.00005/token = $2.50
- Total (example session + keepalives): $9.34 (pre-discount/taxes)

Notes:
- The per-token rates above are illustrative — actual per-token price depends on model family and whether you're on Hosted vs Dedicated.
- For sessions with heavy prefix reuse we apply a cache credit row that subtracts repeated prefix tokens from billable input; the sample sheet shows the exact math with overlapping prefixes.

I've attached the spreadsheet with three permutations (hosted vs dedicated, committed vs on-demand) and a CSV pilot matrix. If you want, we can convert the slab proration into a flat monthly amortized line for your PO to keep invoices simpler.

CCing Kimberly (sales) and Vanessa (account lead) to propose a formal pilot concession.

Cheers,
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie — quick commercial proposal to make procurement simpler.

Proposal (6-month pilot):
- Committed token volume: 18M tokens/month at a 15% pilot discount off standard committed tiers.
- Context-slab handling: convert context-slab charges to a single amortized monthly line item capped at 2x average daily slab for the pilot period. This avoids per-session slab lines on invoices.
- Microfloor: waived for the pilot.
- PO/terms: 30-day net; we can accept a PO referencing deal PLX-2026-09.

If that works for you, we will:
- Produce a sample PO-ready invoice line set (one page) and attach an editable PO_template.pdf for your procurement team.
- Lock pricing in for 6 months; if usage exceeds committed volume we auto-bill overage at the next tier rate (with a 10% safety cap).

Marcus — please review the amortization cap and confirm it aligns with finance constraints.

Sophie — if you approve, we'll prepare a DocuSign for signature and a one-page invoice template for your PO team.
